monitoring.title: Real-Time Water Monitoring
monitoring.subtitle: Continuous supervision platform for water supply systems in the municipalities of Silvanópolis and Miranorte, in the State of Tocantins.
monitoring.smart_city_text: Integrated with the Smart City 4.0 concept, this system connects physical infrastructure to a digital intelligence layer — sensors, telemetry and real-time analysis — to make public management more efficient, transparent and responsive. All processes are continuously and permanently supervised by artificial intelligence algorithms that monitor operational patterns, automatically identify deviations and anomalies, and issue immediate alerts to designated managers or technicians — ensuring each occurrence is handled by the right person, at the right time, before it becomes a critical issue for the population.
monitoring.data_decision_text: Municipal managers and technical teams monitor reservoir levels, pump flow rates and daily production without relying on on-site inspections — reducing operational costs and response time to failures or pressure drops.
monitoring.incident_text: Anomalies in consumption patterns or pump failures are automatically detected. The team is alerted in real time and can act before a supply disruption affects the population — ensuring continuity of the essential treated water service.
monitoring.sustainability_text: Precise pump control reduces electricity consumption and water waste. With historical data and trend projections, management can plan preventive maintenance and investments based on concrete evidence.

diag.title: Condition analysis · {site}
diag.no_data: Waiting for enough telemetry for this analysis.
diag.basis: Limits follow standards and guidance from regulators (ABNT, Brazilian Ministry of Health, ANA, SNIS, US EPA, Ohio EPA, Georgia EPD, Ten States Standards), technical bodies (Hydraulic Institute, ISO, IWA, NIST) and private operator and manufacturer practice (Sabesp, Grundfos). They are published starting points — confirm them against each reservoir's and pump's design.
diag.method_what_text: A single rating of the town's supply system (reservoirs, wells and telemetry), derived from seven families of indicators computed from the last 24 h of telemetry.
diag.method_rule_critical: any indicator critical → the system is CRITICAL
diag.method_rule_good: all indicators normal → the system is NORMAL
diag.method_rule_warning: anything else → the system needs ATTENTION
diag.method_inputs_text: Reserve and level trend, daily water turnover, production continuity, pump flow stability, statistical production anomalies and telemetry freshness.
diag.method_number_text: Each indicator yields a score s from 0 to 100 (100 at the ideal value, 0 at its critical limit). The index H is the weighted mean of those scores; weights (reserve 0.30 · continuity 0.20 · trend 0.15 · turnover 0.10 · stability 0.10 · telemetry 0.10 · anomalies 0.05) are split equally between reservoirs and re-normalised over what could be measured.
diag.method_caveat: These are published reference values, not this network's specification. The 8 h design autonomy is theoretical: use each reservoir's actual volume and demand curve when available.
diag.notes_level: Reservoir level answers two questions: how much water is left to supply the town if production stops (reserve), and whether water is renewed often enough to keep the chlorine residual (quality). The indicators below apply the standards' limits to this reservoir.
diag.notes_flow: Each well/pump's flow shows whether the set is running near its duty point. Large swings mean operation outside the pump's preferred region (more vibration, wear and energy use) or trouble in the well.
diag.notes_production: Hourly and daily production measure supply continuity — what ANA calls intermittency. Stopped hours and statistically anomalous hours are treated separately: stopping is availability; an anomaly is a departure from normal behaviour.
diag.reserve_desc: Current reservoir level, converted into hours of design autonomy.
diag.reserve_model: Distribution reservoirs are sized to hold 1/3 of the maximum-day consumption — 8 h of supply with continuous inflow. Each level percentage point is therefore worth 8 h/100 of theoretical autonomy. The lower part of the tank is the emergency reserve.
diag.reserve_basis: < 25 % (< 2 h): only the emergency reserve is left — low-level alarm. 25–50 % (2–4 h): less than half of the equalisation reserve. 50–80 %: normal equalisation band. 80–95 %: full operating reserve. ≥ 95 %: overflow risk (high-level alarm).
diag.reserve_good: {level} % — full operating reserve, about {autonomy} h of design autonomy.
diag.reserve_watch: {level} % — outside the ideal 80–95 % band: below it the tank is still equalising demand; above {overflow} % it risks overflowing.
diag.reserve_warning: {level} % — less than half the reserve: only {autonomy} h of theoretical autonomy if production stops.
diag.reserve_critical: {level} % — below {critical} %: only the emergency reserve is left, about {autonomy} h of theoretical autonomy.
diag.reserve_action_watch: Follow the level recovery; above {overflow} %, check the pump cut-off control and the overflow.
diag.reserve_action_warning: Confirm the pumps feeding this tank are running and compare production with demand.
diag.reserve_action_critical: Alert operations: check pumps, power and trunk main; consider valve operations to prioritise critical areas.
diag.trend_desc: Hours until the level reaches the critical reserve ({critical} %) at the current rate of change.
diag.trend_model: The rate dL/dt is the slope of the least-squares line over the last 3 h of readings. If the level is falling, t = (L − Lc)/abs(dL/dt); if it is rising or steady there is no depletion horizon.
diag.trend_basis: < 2 h: emptying imminent. 2–6 h: time for one intervention only. 6–12 h: watch. ≥ 12 h or rising: normal. The target Lc is the emergency-reserve limit used by low-level alarms.
diag.trend_good: Level steady or rising ({slope} %/h) — no risk of reaching the critical reserve in the next 12 h.
diag.trend_watch: Level falling {slope} %/h — critical reserve in about {hours} h.
diag.trend_warning: Level falling {slope} %/h — critical reserve in only {hours} h.
diag.trend_critical: Level falling {slope} %/h — critical reserve in {hours} h or less.
diag.trend_action_watch: Check whether the fall matches the demand peak; if it persists, check the pumps.
diag.trend_action_warning: Confirm pump start and inflow; prepare valve operations.
diag.trend_action_critical: Immediate action: demand exceeds production — check pumps, power and leaks.
diag.turnover_desc: Level fluctuation over the last 24 h — an estimate of the share of volume renewed per day.
diag.turnover_model: For a constant cross-section, the share of volume exchanged per day ≈ ΔL = Lmax − Lmin (in % of useful depth). Estimated turnover time is Tren = 100/ΔL days. Stagnant water ages, loses chlorine residual and favours microbial growth.
diag.turnover_basis: Ohio EPA requires ≥ 20 % daily turnover (25 % recommended); Georgia EPD asks for at least 30 %; Ten States requires turnover within 5 days (≡ 20 %/day). Brazil's Portaria GM/MS 888/2021 requires ≥ 0.2 mg/L free chlorine in reservoirs too. ≥ 30 %: normal · 20–30 %: watch · 10–20 %: attention · < 10 %: critical.
diag.turnover_watch: {pct} %/day turnover (≈ {days} days) — meets the 20 % minimum, below the 30 % goal.
diag.turnover_warning: {pct} %/day turnover (≈ {days} days) — below the 20 %/day minimum: risk of losing chlorine residual.
diag.turnover_critical: Only {pct} %/day turnover — water nearly stagnant (≈ {days} days).
diag.turnover_action_watch: Consider widening the operating band (let the level drop further before restarting pumps).
diag.turnover_action_warning: Measure chlorine residual at the tank outlet and widen the daily level swing.
diag.turnover_action_critical: Sample chlorine residual and consider forced renewal; review level control.
diag.continuity_desc: Share of meter-hours with production in the last 24 h ({up} of {total}).
diag.continuity_model: Availability D = Σ operating hours / Σ observed hours × 100, summed over all the town's meters. An hour counts as operating when production exceeds 5 % of that meter's hourly maximum (same rule as the anomaly model).
diag.continuity_basis: Availability = uptime / (uptime + downtime) — ISO 14224. ANA (NR 9/2024) and SNIS (IN071–IN074) track supply stoppages and intermittency. ≥ 90 %: normal · 75–90 %: watch · 50–75 %: attention · < 50 %: critical. Standby pumps kept off by design lower this number — bear that in mind.
diag.continuity_good: {pct} % of hours with production — continuous supply.
diag.continuity_watch: {pct} % of hours with production — some stops in the period.
diag.continuity_warning: {pct} % of hours with production — frequent stops: risk of intermittent supply.
diag.continuity_critical: Only {pct} % of hours with production — production stopped most of the day.
diag.continuity_action_watch: Check whether stops were scheduled (level control, peak tariff hours).
diag.continuity_action_warning: Find the stopped meters in the values list and check power and starters.
diag.continuity_action_critical: Call maintenance: pumps stopped for long periods compromise supply.
diag.stability_desc: Highest coefficient of variation of running flow among the pumps (worst: {meter}).
diag.stability_model: CV = σ/μ × 100 over running readings (flow > 5 % of max). By Shewhart's rule 99.7 % of readings fall within μ ± 3σ. For the lower limit to stay inside the pump's preferred region (70 % of duty flow), 3·CV ≤ 30 % is needed, i.e. CV ≤ 10 %.
diag.stability_basis: Hydraulic Institute ANSI/HI 9.6.3: preferred operating region between 70 % and 120 % of best-efficiency flow; outside it vibration, wear and energy use grow (Grundfos). < 5 %: normal · 5–10 %: watch · 10–20 %: attention · ≥ 20 %: critical.
diag.stability_good: CV {pct} % ({meter}) — stable flows, pumps near their duty point.
diag.stability_watch: CV {pct} % ({meter}) — noticeable variation, still inside the preferred region.
diag.stability_warning: CV {pct} % ({meter}) — the pump swings outside its preferred operating region.
diag.stability_action_warning: Check well drawdown, air entry, valves and the flow sensor.
diag.stability_action_critical: Inspect pump and well (cavitation, clogging, meter failure).
diag.anomalies_desc: Hours with statistically abnormal production in the last 24 h.
diag.anomalies_model: For each meter, running hours form a distribution. An hour is anomalous when it falls outside Tukey's fences [Q1 − 1.5·IQR; Q3 + 1.5·IQR] and deviates more than 30 % from the median. Stopped hours are excluded (they belong to continuity).
diag.anomalies_basis: Tukey fences (NIST/SEMATECH 7.1.6) and Shewhart ±3σ control limits (NIST 6.3.2). 0 h: normal · 1–2 h: watch · 3–5 h: attention · ≥ 6 h: critical.
diag.anomalies_good: No anomalous hours — production within its statistical pattern.
diag.anomalies_critical: {n} anomalous hours — unstable production throughout the day.
diag.anomalies_action_watch: Check the alerts below the production chart.
diag.anomalies_action_warning: Investigate the listed hours (power dips, valve operations, metering faults).
diag.anomalies_action_critical: Assess the motor-pump set and the meter; production is not stable.
diag.telemetry_desc: Age of the latest reading of the town's most delayed sensor ({sensor}).
diag.telemetry_model: Δt = now − time of last reading, for every level and flow sensor; the worst counts. Without recent readings the other indicators stop reflecting reality.
diag.telemetry_basis: Ten States Standards §7.4.3: level control by telemetry with low-level and overflow alarms; operators such as Sabesp supervise reservoirs and pumping in real time. Sensors report about every minute: ≤ 10 min: normal · 10–30 min: watch · 30–60 min: attention · > 60 min: critical.
diag.telemetry_good: All sensors up to date — oldest latest reading {min} min ago.
diag.telemetry_warning: {sensor} silent for {min} min — partly blind operation.
diag.telemetry_critical: {sensor} silent for {min} min — no visibility of this point.
diag.telemetry_action_watch: Keep watching; may be a brief communication delay.
diag.telemetry_action_warning: Check the device's power/battery and signal.
diag.telemetry_action_critical: Send a crew: sensor or gateway is down.

energisa.about_lead: Industry 4.0 was about automation, interconnection and data-driven optimisation — efficiency and productivity. Industry 5.0 keeps that technological base and adds three pillars the European Commission defined in 2021.

diag.basis: Default thresholds follow the documents below. They are starting points, not a specification — confirm each against your own asset rating and your utility's practice.
diag.harmonics_action_warning: Identify the non-linear loads and consider filtering; derate the transformer if distortion persists.
diag.harmonics_desc: Total harmonic distortion of the current waveform. Harmonics heat the windings and neutral without contributing to delivered power.
diag.harmonics_warning: {thd}% distortion is high. Expect extra winding and neutral heating beyond what the loading figure suggests.
diag.harmonics_watch: {thd}% distortion, typical of non-linear loads such as drives and switched supplies.
diag.loading_action_critical: Transfer load or replace the unit. Sustained overload shortens life disproportionately.
diag.loading_action_warning: Review the growth trend and plan load transfer or an uprate before the next peak season.
diag.loading_critical: {pct}% exceeds the nameplate rating. Insulation life is being consumed rapidly.
diag.loading_desc: Apparent power drawn as a share of the transformer nameplate rating ({nominal} kVA). It is the primary driver of insulation ageing.
diag.loading_good: At {pct}% the unit has ample headroom. Ageing is nominal and short overloads can be absorbed.
diag.loading_warning: {pct}% leaves little reserve. Peaks will push the unit into overload and accelerate ageing.
diag.loading_watch: {pct}% is a normal working load. Worth watching if demand keeps growing.
diag.method_caveat: These are published defaults, not a specification for your fleet. A utility sets its own operating limits, and an individual unit may be rated differently — confirm against the nameplate and your internal practice before acting on a rating.
diag.method_inputs_text: Loading, temperature, phase balance, supply voltage, power factor and current distortion. An indicator that cannot be measured — no temperature probe, current too low to analyse — is skipped rather than counted as healthy.
diag.method_number_text: Each indicator also produces a 0–100 score — 100 at the ideal value, 0 at its critical limit. Those scores are combined by weight: loading and temperature carry most of it because they drive insulation ageing directly, power factor least because it is a commercial concern rather than a physical one. Weights are re-normalised over the indicators that could actually be measured.
diag.method_number_vs_label: The number and the rating are deliberately independent: the number shows how much margin is left overall, while the rating above follows the worst single indicator. A transformer can therefore read a comfortable number and still be CRITICAL — that is the point.
diag.method_rule_critical: any indicator critical → the asset is CRITICAL
diag.method_rule_good: every indicator normal → the asset is NORMAL
diag.method_rule_warning: anything else → the asset needs ATTENTION
diag.method_what_text: A single condition rating for the transformer, derived from six independent measurements taken from the live telemetry. It is not a score out of 100 averaged together — averaging lets one critical reading hide behind five healthy ones.
diag.method_where_text: Each indicator carries its own thresholds and the document they come from. Open "How this was calculated" on any card to see the formula, the values used, and the full scale with the current reading marked.
diag.no_data: Waiting for device telemetry. Analysis appears once the transformer reports.
diag.powerFactor_action_warning: Install or repair power factor correction. Excess reactive current also wastes capacity and adds heating.
diag.powerFactor_action_watch: Identify the inductive loads responsible; capacitor correction usually pays back quickly.
diag.powerFactor_desc: Ratio of useful power to total power drawn. Below the {floor} floor, utilities bill the excess reactive energy.
diag.powerFactor_good: {pf} is above the {floor} floor. No reactive surcharge applies.
diag.powerFactor_warning: {pf} is well below the {floor} floor, with {reactive} kvar of reactive demand inflating current for no useful work.
diag.powerFactor_watch: {pf} is below the {floor} floor, drawing {reactive} kvar. Reactive billing may apply.
diag.thermal_action_critical: Reduce load immediately and inspect. Prolonged operation risks insulation failure.
diag.thermal_action_warning: Check for blocked cooling, and correlate with loading to separate overload from a cooling fault.
diag.thermal_critical: {temp} °C is at or above the {limit} °C limit. Every hour here costs disproportionate insulation life.
diag.thermal_desc: Measured operating temperature. Insulation ageing roughly doubles for every 6–8 °C above the rated hot-spot.
diag.thermal_good: {temp} °C is comfortably within the operating band.
diag.thermal_warning: {temp} °C is high. Ageing is accelerating measurably at this temperature.
diag.thermal_watch: {temp} °C is elevated. Check whether it tracks load or persists after load drops.
diag.title: Condition analysis
diag.unbalance_action_critical: Inspect the lightly loaded phase for an open connection or blown protection, then rebalance the feeders.
diag.unbalance_action_warning: Redistribute single-phase loads across phases at the next maintenance window.
diag.unbalance_critical: Severe {pct}% unbalance: CH{high} draws {highValue} A while CH{low} draws only {lowValue} A. The transformer heats without delivering proportional power, and the lightly loaded phase may indicate a disconnected or failed feeder.
diag.unbalance_desc: Greatest deviation of any phase current from the three-phase mean. Unbalance drives neutral current and heats the transformer without delivering useful power.
diag.unbalance_good: Phases are within {pct}% of each other — well balanced.
diag.unbalance_warning: {pct}% unbalance. CH{high} at {highValue} A against CH{low} at {lowValue} A produces neutral current and extra heating.
diag.unbalance_watch: {pct}% deviation. CH{high} carries {highValue} A while CH{low} carries {lowValue} A.
diag.voltage_action_critical: Investigate immediately — verify tap position, conductor sizing and upstream regulation.
diag.voltage_action_warning: Check tap setting and feeder loading; persistent deviation may require a tap change.
diag.voltage_critical: {volts} V is {deviation}% from nominal — a critical excursion. Connected equipment is at risk and the deviation is reportable.
diag.voltage_desc: Mean delivered voltage against the {nominal} V nominal. Regulators define adequate, precarious and critical bands; sustained excursions are reportable.
diag.voltage_good: {volts} V ({deviation}% from nominal) sits in the adequate band, {low}–{high} V.
diag.voltage_warning: {volts} V is {deviation}% from nominal, outside the adequate band of {low}–{high} V.

energisa.page_intro: Low-voltage monitoring of pole-mounted distribution transformers. IoT sensing and AI analysis are the Industry 4.0 foundation; what makes this 5.0 is what the data is for — supporting the field engineer instead of replacing them, extending asset life instead of replacing equipment, and keeping supply standing when conditions turn.
energisa.pillar_human_text: Industry 4.0 treats people as operators of automated systems. Here every indicator shows its formula, its inputs and its scale, so the engineer can check the machine rather than obey it. The analysis proposes; the person decides.
energisa.pillar_resilience_text: Continuous condition data turns a run-to-fail network into a maintainable one. Knowing which unit is degrading, before it fails, is what keeps supply standing through load growth and extreme weather.
energisa.pillar_sustainability_text: Detecting phase imbalance, reactive excess and harmonic distortion recovers capacity that is already installed. A transformer kept inside its thermal band lasts decades longer — the greenest asset is the one not replaced.
energisa.range_invalid: The end must be after the start.

wave.harmonics_critical: Voltage distortion {dttV} % exceeds the PRODIST 10 % limit. Distortion is affecting delivered quality, not just the transformer.
wave.harmonics_desc: Decomposes the wave into multiples of the 60 Hz fundamental. Beyond the total, the dominant order points at the cause: the 3rd is typical of single-phase non-linear loads and adds in the neutral; the 5th and 7th of three-phase rectifiers.
wave.harmonics_good: Voltage distortion {dttV} % and current THD {thdI} % — clean spectrum.
wave.harmonics_unknown: No waveform available to compute the spectrum.
wave.harmonics_warning: Current THD {thdI} % on CH{channel}, dominated by order {order}. Expect extra winding and neutral heating beyond what loading indicates.
wave.harmonics_watch: Current THD {thdI} % on CH{channel}, dominated by order {order}. Typical of switched supplies and drives.
wave.phasor_critical: {drift}° drift from 120° on pair {worst} — phase sequence compromised. Check connections and the lightly loaded phase.
wave.phasor_desc: Places each phase fundamental on the plane. Two independent readings: the separation between voltages, which should be 120° in a balanced system, and the angle φ between voltage and current on each phase, whose cosine is the power factor.
wave.phasor_good: Phases separated within {drift}° of the theoretical 120° — balanced sequence.
wave.phasor_unknown: Not enough phasors to assess the sequence.
wave.phasor_warning: {drift}° drift from 120° on pair {worst}. Points at uneven phase loading or a faulty connection.
wave.phasor_watch: {drift}° drift from 120° on pair {worst}. Still tolerable, worth watching.
wave.temporal_critical: Crest factor {crest} on CH{channel} — severe current distortion.
wave.temporal_desc: Compares the measured wave against an ideal sinusoid. Crest factor (peak ÷ RMS) is the discriminator: a pure sine is √2 ≈ 1.41. Rectifier loads draw current in short spikes and raise it; saturation flattens the top and lowers it.
wave.temporal_good: Crest factor {crest} on CH{channel}, close to {ideal} — essentially sinusoidal.
wave.temporal_unknown: Not enough current to assess the waveform.
wave.temporal_warning: Crest factor {crest} on CH{channel}, well above {ideal}. Current flows in short spikes: heating exceeds what the RMS value suggests.
wave.temporal_watch: Crest factor {crest} on CH{channel} deviates from {ideal}. Suggests a moderate non-linear load or the onset of flat-topping.
